post.caption: Jewel likely began as a Latin joke. Most dictionaries trace it to jocus, the Latin word for game. It reached English from French, as jouel, around the year 1300. Gem comes from the Latin word for a bud. Americans write jewelry, and the British write jewellery. In a watch, a jewel is a tiny ruby or sapphire bearing. A hard jewel keeps a pivot hole from wearing out of shape. An English patent from 1704 covered piercing rubies for watches. A typical mechanical watch has about 17 jewels. Bijou probably comes from a Breton word for finger ring.
